stories.headline: 5.3 magnitude earthquake strikes Afghanistan: NCS
stories.title: 5.3 magnitude earthquake strikes Afghanistan: NCS
stories.summary: Kabul , October 1 : An earthquake of magnitude 5.3 struck Afghanistan on Thursday morning, the National Centre for Seismology (NCS) said. According to the NCS, the earthquake occurred at 6:59:20 am IST at a depth of 126 km. In a post shared on X, the NCS said, "EQ of M: 5.3, On: 01/10/2026 06:59:20 IST, Lat: 35.981 N, Long: 68.700 E, Depth: 126 Km, Location: Afghanistan." The NCS located the earthquake at latitude 35.981 North and longitude 68.700 East, around 165 km NNW of Kabul. Further details are awaited.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

stories.headline: Flood crisis deepens in Bihar as embankments breached by Gandak River across multiple districts
stories.title: Flood crisis deepens in Bihar as embankments breached by Gandak River across multiple districts
stories.summary: Movement has also been affected in West Champaran, where floodwaters have reached the Machhargawan area.
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: wire echo (ians) -> no independent boost

opening: Movement has also been affected in West Champaran, where floodwaters have reached the Machhargawan area.
Patna, Oct 1: The flood situation in Bihar has worsened following heavy rainfall in Nepal’s Gandak basin, with the river swelling sharply and embankments breached at several locations.
body: Around 2.03 lakh people across six districts are reported to have been affected, with West Champaran, Saran, Gopalganj and Muzaffarpur among the worst-hit areas.
The Water Resources Department had recorded a discharge of 5.435 lakh cusecs at the Valmikinagar Gandak Barrage, with the flow remaining above 5 lakh cusecs for several hours.
The surge has put further pressure on embankments and low-lying areas downstream.
In Saran, the right Saran embankment of the Gandak near Haijalpur in Maker block was damaged during the intervening night of Tuesday and Wednesday.
Reports also indicated damage near Baghakol, with floodwaters entering nearby low-lying areas.
A house in Haijalpur village was reportedly swept away by the strong current after the embankment gave way.
Floodwaters spread across several villages, forcing residents to move to embankments, rooftops and other safer locations.
Water from the Gandak has also reached the NH-722 area near Maker, disrupting movement and raising concerns for villages along the affected stretch.
In Gopalganj's Baikunthpur block, the Bandhauli-Sheetalpur-Faizullahpur Zamindari Bund was breached at Sheetalpur amid intense pressure from the swollen Gandak.
According to the Water Resources Department, the initial breach was around six metres wide.
Floodwaters threatened low-lying areas around Parsauni, Sheetalpur and Pakhan, with the breach putting several surrounding villages at risk.
The situation also deteriorated in Muzaffarpur, where an old Gandak embankment at Jaimal Dumri in Paru block was breached.
Floodwaters subsequently spread towards nearby residential areas, prompting residents to move to safer and higher locations.
Local reports said water entered homes and roads in the affected area, while rescue and monitoring operations were intensified by the administration.
Several areas of West Champaran remain severely affected after breaches in the Gandak embankment system.
Bagaha, Bairia and Yogapatti are among the areas facing inundation, with residents taking shelter on roads, embankments and at relief centres.
The Gandak had earlier reached a record 91.25 metres at the Bagaha gauge, exceeding the previous high of 90.90 metres recorded in 2024.
Floodwaters have also disrupted road connectivity at several locations.
The Chhapra-Sattarghat route has been affected, while water has accumulated on stretches of the Areraj-Hajipur road, disrupting traffic.
The rising water level of the Ganga has added to concerns in other parts of Bihar, with the river rising in the Patna-Begusarai-Khagaria belt.
Several ghats in Patna have again been affected by rising water.
The expanding flood situation has placed additional pressure on the administration to maintain rescue operations, monitor vulnerable embankments and ensure relief supplies reach affected communities.
In Saran, District Magistrate Vaibhav Srivastava and SSP Roshan Kumar inspected affected areas and directed officials to intensify relief and rescue operations.

With the Gandak continuing to remain swollen and multiple embankments under pressure, authorities across the affected districts are maintaining close watch on river levels and vulnerable stretches while relief and rescue operations continue.
--IANS.

stories.headline: Bank's Fear That Borrower May Flee Country Can't Alone Justify LOC In Perpetuity: Delhi High Court
stories.title: Bank's Fear That Borrower May Flee Country Can't Alone Justify LOC In Perpetuity: Delhi High Court
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Delhi High Court has held that a bank's apprehension that a borrower may flee the country or that its financial claim may be jeopardised cannot, by itself, justify the indefinite continuation of a Look Out Circular (LOC).

Justice Amit Mahajan made the observation while quashing an LOC issued against one Rajat Gupta at the instance of Bank of Baroda in connection with a criminal case arising from loan accounts classified as non-performing assets and subsequently declared fraudulent.

“In the above context, the apprehension expressed by the Bank that the Petitioner may flee the country or financial claim of the Bank cannot be the sole reason to warrant continuation of an LOC in perpetuity, that too when the LOC issued at the instance of CBI has already been suspended,” the Court observed.
The Court noted that the investigation was completed and the CBI had filed four chargesheets, on which the trial court had taken cognisance.

It further observed that Gupta's travel was already subject to the supervision of the trial court, which had granted him bail with conditions, including the requirement to seek permission before travelling abroad.
Gupta, a former director of Govardhan Industries Pvt.
Ltd., had approached the Court seeking quashing of the LOC issued at the instance of the bank.
He submitted that he was engaged in the business of Ayurvedic medicines and needed to travel to Kazakhstan for business purposes.
Despite his requests, the bank had not withdrawn or suspended the LOC.
The Court noted that Gupta had previously been granted permission to travel abroad and had not misused the liberty granted to him.

Holding that an LOC is a coercive measure that cannot be issued or continued routinely merely because a person is facing trial, the Court observed that no material was placed before it to demonstrate that Gupta was likely to abscond.
The Court accordingly quashed the LOC issued at the instance of Bank of Baroda, observing that the LOC issued at the instance of CBI already stood suspended.

stories.headline: No Election Commissioner has dissented on any decision since Feb 2025: Sources
stories.title: No Election Commissioner has dissented on any decision since Feb 2025: Sources
stories.summary: No Election Commissioner has dissented on any decision since Feb 2025: Sources
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: As questions grow over dissent within the EC over SIR, sources in the poll panel have said its three members have taken every decision unanimously since February 19, 2025, even as a media report highlighted 14 objections recorded by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi over various aspects of the exercise.
Amid questions over dissent in the Election Commission and its handling of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, sources in the poll panel on Thursday told India Today that no.
Election Commissioner has dissented on any decision since February 19, 2025.

The assertion comes a week after The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally recorded their objections 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders concerning the SIR process under Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

According to the report, the objections covered several aspects of the exercise, including the centralisation of the ECINet electoral roll database platform, changes to Form 6 and decisions on deletion of names from electoral rolls.
The issue has gained further attention as INDIA bloc parties met to discuss the SIR exercise and raised questions over the Election Commission's functioning.

The poll panel, however, maintains that SIR is a statutory and established process for revision of electoral rolls and sources said that all decisions taken by the three-member poll panel since February 19, 2025, have been unanimous.
According to the EC, the central objective of SIR is to identify dead, duplicate, fake and shifted voters while ensuring that all eligible voters remain on the electoral rolls.
While answering the questions about Form 6, which is used by new voters and those seeking to add their names to the electoral rolls, the EC sources said that there has been no change in the form.
On the legal scrutiny of SIR, the commission sources pointed to the Supreme Court's proceedings, saying the court has never suspended the exercise.
The sources said the court allowed SIR to proceed, including the voter declaration and mapping process, while putting safeguards in place for voters.
The poll panel has described SIR as a comprehensive process that has been followed for years.

stories.headline: Delhi High Court Seeks Appointment Records Of Bar Council Returning Officer In Plea Challenging BCD Election Schedule
stories.title: Delhi High Court Seeks Appointment Records Of Bar Council Returning Officer In Plea Challenging BCD Election Schedule
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Delhi High Court has sought documents relating to the appointment and tenure of the Returning Officer conducting the upcoming election for the office-bearers of the Bar Council of Delhi (BCD), including its member representative to the Bar Council of India.
Justice Saurabh Banerjee passed the order while dealing with a petition filed by lawyer Mehmood Pracha, challenging a notice issued...
an affordable subscription scheme!!!
Justice Saurabh Banerjee passed the order while dealing with a petition filed by lawyer Mehmood Pracha, challenging a notice issued on September 25, which had scheduled the election for October 10.

Pracha, appearing in person, also sought a direction to the Returning Officer- Senior Advocate Rakesh Munjal, to convene an extraordinary meeting pursuant to a requisition dated September 26, under Rule 54 of the Bar Council of Delhi Rules, 1963.
The Court noted that the principal issue raised in the petition concerned the authority of the Returning Officer, who issued the impugned notice prescribing the election schedule.

In view of this issue, the Court directed the parties to place on record the letter of appointment and all requisite connected documents concerning the Returning Officer's appointment, particularly those relating to the subsistence and period of his tenure.

“As such, learned (senior) counsel for the parties seek, and are granted, a period of two weeks for filing the said Letter of Appointment and/ or all such requisite connected document(s) qua the appointment of the said respondent no.2, specifying the period/ tenure of his appointment…,” the Court said.

It also directed the partied to file a two-page note of submissions, along with duly highlighted judgments setting out the propositions of law relied upon, and any other documents they seek to rely upon, within three days.

Although the Court did not issue notice in the plea as of now, it clarified that Pracha, being an elected member of the Bar Council of Delhi, is entitled to file his nomination in accordance with law.
The matter has been listed for hearing now on October 06.

stories.headline: Madras High Court refuses to reject election petition filed against Esakki Subaya’s Ambasamudram win
stories.title: Madras High Court refuses to reject election petition filed against Esakki Subaya’s Ambasamudram win
stories.summary: Justice P.B. Balaji dismisses an application filed by the resigned MLA, who had shifted allegiance from the AIADMK to the TVK, to reject the election petition filed by a voter
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Madras High Court on Thursday (October 1, 2026) refused to reject an election petition filed by a voter challenging the victory of Esakki Subaya from the Ambasamudram Legislative Assembly constituency during the general elections conducted earlier this year.

Justice P.B. Balaji dismissed an application filed by Mr. Subaya, who had won as an All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) candidate but resigned from his MLA post before joining the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), to reject the election petition preferred by Kanthimathinathan.
The judge, however, allowed another application filed by the resigned MLA to reject certain pleadings made by the election petitioner in his plea.

The refusal to reject the election petition assumes significance in light of the fact that Ambasamudram was one of the five constituencies where byelections had been stalled by a Division Bench of the High Court due to pending election petitions.

Pursuant to the interim stay order passed by the Division Bench in a public interest litigation (PIL) petition on July 10, 2026, the ECI had filed a counter affidavit in response to the PIL petition stating that it, too, does not intend to conduct bypolls to the five constituencies: Tiruchi East, Perundurai, Ambasamudram, Viralimalai, and Karur.

However, after the filing of the counter affidavit, Justice D. Bharatha Chakravarthy of the High Court on September 8, 2026, rejected the election petition filed against the victory of S. Jayakumar, who also had won as an AIADMK candidate but resigned from his MLA post before joining the TVK.

Hence, in the written submissions filed before the first Division Bench comprising Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan during the final hearing on the PIL petition, the ECI urged the Bench to exempt Perundurai alone from its interim stay order.

The ECI told the court that byelection could be conducted for the Perundurai constituency as the election petition had been rejected, if the Supreme Court does not grant any stay and if the Division Bench exempts that constituency alone from the five constituencies where bypolls had been stalled.
The present refusal to reject the election petition with respect to the Ambasamudram constituency might delay the conduct of bypolls in the constituency.

stories.headline: Kerala HC denies plea by Pakistani national married to Indian man seeking visa to enter country
stories.title: Kerala HC denies plea by Pakistani national married to Indian man seeking visa to enter country
stories.summary: Court holds that due to government order still in force suspending all visa services to Pakistani nationals after Pahalgam terror attack, the petitioner cannot demand that her visa application be processed
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'terror attack' in summary weight 50.4
article_sentences: The Kerala High Court recently ruled that a Pakistani national could not demand that the government consider her visa application even if she was married to an Indian citizen.

Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas found that due to the government order that was still in force suspending all visa services to Pakistani nationals after the Pahalgam terror attack, the petitioner could not demand that her visa application be processed.
The court stated that no foreign national, even if married to an Indian citizen, had a “vested right” to demand that the person be permitted to enter the country.
The petitioner had sought to apply for an Indian visa to attend her brother-in-law’s wedding.
However, when she attempted to apply for an Indian visa, she could not identify a procedure to obtain any suitable visa.

They contended that the petitioner had done no harm to the nation and that declining an opportunity to apply for and process a visa violated the right to equality and the right to life guaranteed by the Constitution to all persons, not only citizens.
The Centre contended that no foreign national could claim permission to enter or remain in India as a matter of right, except according to law or policy decisions of the Central government.
It argued that the Centre could regulate immigration at its discretion in the interest of the nation.
The Centre maintained that fresh long-term visas were not open for consideration and that even such prior visas were permitted only until April 29, 2025.
Unless the petitioner attained Indian citizenship, she could not apply or have her application processed, since she was a Pakistani national.
The court held that the regulation of entry, stay, movement and departure of foreigners into and from India was an “exclusive sovereign function” of the Centre.
The government order issued in April 2025 after the Pahalgam attacks revoked all existing visas for Pakistani nationals and stated that new visas would not be permitted.

stories.headline: Cafe 3 norms: India shifts gears on EVs, opens road for multiple powertrains
stories.title: Cafe 3 norms: India shifts gears on EVs, opens road for multiple powertrains
stories.summary: After nearly 30 months, multiple drafts and a lobbying war that reached the Prime Minister’s Office, India has notified its third set of fuel-efficiency rules for cars that will decide the kind of products carmakers will develop over the coming years.The final Corporate Average Fuel Efficiency, or Cafe, norms come into effect from April next year and seek 16.7 percent better efficiency from new cars by 2032. The government has allowed carmakers to get there by almost any road: Electric vehicles (EVs), range extenders, ethanol, hybrids, or others.Unlike other emission norms such as Bharat Stage, Cafe applies to a carmaker’s entire fleet instead of individual cars.When a carmaker calculates its fleet average, cleaner vehicles are multiplied. Under the final Cafe norms, an EV sold will count as three cars, as will a range extender. Plug-in hybrids and flex-fuel strong hybrids will count as 2.5 cars, strong hybrids as 1.6 and flex-fuel vehicles as 1.1 cars.The first draft from April 2024 that was made public in June had proposed a higher—4 times—benefit for EVs and there was no mention of range extenders. The benefit for hybrids was lower, with plug-ins at 2 and strong hybrids at 1.2. The maximum concession was for hydrogen fuel cell cars at 5, which have disappeared from the final list.The surprise entry is the range extender, or range-extended electric vehicle (REEV), which is practically an EV with a small combustion engine that only works as a generator to charge the battery. No carmaker currently sells REEVs in India but almost all of them are developing this tech. JSW-MG unveiled a platform in July that can be used to develop range extenders while Suzuki talked about it in its latest Technology Strategy briefing.Also Read: In defense of small cars: Why Maruti Suzuki is pushing for less stringent fuel efficiency norms“We are likely to see several range extender launches, as they combine the benefits of electrification with the convenience of longer range and reduced charging concerns,” says Puneet Gupta, director at Mobility Global. This makes range extenders particularly attractive for larger vehicles and long-distance driving, he adds.Cafe norms were first introduced in 2017 and a second iteration came in 2022. The latest norms come into effect from April 1, 2027, and will run till March 31, 2032.Amitabh Kant, former CEO of Niti Aayog who helped shape India’s early EV push, calls the norms “a huge missed opportunity”. “The new Cafe norms are backward looking at worst and status quoist at best,” he wrote on X. “EVs become one option among many, when they should be the destination.”The Cafe regime is shifting the focus from simply increasing EV penetration to optimising the entire powertrain portfolio, says Vivek Sharma, automotive director at GlobalData Plc.“With BEVs/REEVs, hybrids, flex-fuel, 48V systems and other efficiency technologies offering different routes to compliance, Cafe-III will make powertrain strategy—and the balance between vehicle mix, technology and fleet efficiency—more central than ever to OEM strategy.”For carmakers with predominantly ICE-led portfolios, the framework increases the strategic importance of electrified and alternative-fuel powertrains as part of the overall portfolio mix, according to Som Kapoor, Pratik Shah and Aneesh Ajayan, partners, automotive, EY-Parthenon.Under the new norms, the government will progressively tighten fleet-average fuel-consumption targets, with the benchmark at 3.996 litres per 100 km in 2027-28, falling to 3.3273 litres per 100 km by 2031-32. This represents an improvement of about 16.7 percent in fuel efficiency over the five-year period.The rules also give carmakers more flexibility in emissions compliance. Rather than calculating it annually, the framework introduces two compliance blocks of three years and two years, allowing companies to offset deficits in one year against surpluses generated in another year within the same period.Manufacturers also have the option of purchasing credits from the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) at prices ranging from Rs2,500 to Rs4,500 per g/km. Tata Motors had earlier opposed this; Kant agreed on Wednesday.“How can [the BEE] sell credits? opening: After nearly 30 months, multiple drafts and a lobbying war that reached the Prime Minister’s Office, India has notified its third set of fuel-efficiency rules for cars that will decide the kind of products carmakers will develop over the coming years.
The final Corporate Average Fuel Efficiency, or Cafe, norms come into effect from April next year and seek 16.7 percent better efficiency from new cars by 2032.
body: The government has allowed carmakers to get there by almost any road: Electric vehicles (EVs), range extenders, ethanol, hybrids, or others.
Unlike other emission norms such as Bharat Stage, Cafe applies to a carmaker’s entire fleet instead of individual cars.
When a carmaker calculates its fleet average, cleaner vehicles are multiplied.
Under the final Cafe norms, an EV sold will count as three cars, as will a range extender.
Plug-in hybrids and flex-fuel strong hybrids will count as 2.5 cars, strong hybrids as 1.6 and flex-fuel vehicles as 1.1 cars.
The first draft from April 2024 that was made public in June had proposed a higher—4 times—benefit for EVs and there was no mention of range extenders.
The benefit for hybrids was lower, with plug-ins at 2 and strong hybrids at 1.2.
The maximum concession was for hydrogen fuel cell cars at 5, which have disappeared from the final list.
The surprise entry is the range extender, or range-extended electric vehicle (REEV), which is practically an EV with a small combustion engine that only works as a generator to charge the battery.
No carmaker currently sells REEVs in India but almost all of them are developing this tech.
JSW-MG unveiled a platform in July that can be used to develop range extenders while Suzuki talked about it in its latest Technology Strategy briefing.

“We are likely to see several range extender launches, as they combine the benefits of electrification with the convenience of longer range and reduced charging concerns,” says Puneet Gupta, director at Mobility Global.
This makes range extenders particularly attractive for larger vehicles and long-distance driving, he adds.
Cafe norms were first introduced in 2017 and a second iteration came in 2022.
The latest norms come into effect from April 1, 2027, and will run till March 31, 2032.
Amitabh Kant, former CEO of Niti Aayog who helped shape India’s early EV push, calls the norms “a huge missed opportunity”.

“The new Cafe norms are backward looking at worst and status quoist at best,” he wrote on X. “EVs become one option among many, when they should be the destination.” The Cafe regime is shifting the focus from simply increasing EV penetration to optimising the entire powertrain portfolio, says Vivek Sharma, automotive director at GlobalData Plc.

“With BEVs/REEVs, hybrids, flex-fuel, 48V systems and other efficiency technologies offering different routes to compliance, Cafe-III will make powertrain strategy—and the balance between vehicle mix, technology and fleet efficiency—more central than ever to OEM strategy.” For carmakers with predominantly ICE-led portfolios, the framework increases the strategic importance of electrified and alternative-fuel powertrains as part of the overall portfolio mix, according to Som Kapoor, Pratik Shah and Aneesh Ajayan, partners, automotive, EY-Parthenon.

Under the new norms, the government will progressively tighten fleet-average fuel-consumption targets, with the benchmark at 3.996 litres per 100 km in 2027-28, falling to 3.3273 litres per 100 km by 2031-32.
This represents an improvement of about 16.7 percent in fuel efficiency over the five-year period.
The rules also give carmakers more flexibility in emissions compliance.

Rather than calculating it annually, the framework introduces two compliance blocks of three years and two years, allowing companies to offset deficits in one year against surpluses generated in another year within the same period.
Manufacturers also have the option of purchasing credits from the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) at prices ranging from Rs2,500 to Rs4,500 per g/km.
Tata Motors had earlier opposed this; Kant agreed on Wednesday.
“How can [the BEE] sell credits?
A regulator can’t be a player in the market it regulates,” Kant wrote.
Companies that outperform Cafe targets can generate surplus credits and trade them with other carmakers facing a shortfall.
Another way for carmakers to improve their fleet-level compliance is by using renewable and low-carbon fuels.
Before a car’s tailpipe CO2 goes into the fleet average, it is discounted for the renewable share of the fuel it uses.
For diesel cars, the discount will depend on the actual biofuel blending percentage notified by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.
Carmakers can also deduct 1 g/km each for 12 technologies, capped at 9 g/km.

The list includes start-stop systems, tyre pressure monitoring, regenerative braking, 6-speed or higher transmission, efficient alternators, 12V/48V efficient alternator, 12V/48V motor generator, LED exterior lighting, advanced glass, electric water pumps, high-efficiency air conditioning systems, solar-reflective paint and pulse width modulation-controlled radiator fans.
For the first compliance block—FY28 to FY30—these savings are self-declared by the carmaker.
Only from FY31 must claims be backed by test results generated in accordance with the methodologies and procedures specified by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
The draft norms had divided the auto industry, with the country’s largest carmaker against almost every other large player.
Maruti Suzuki, which makes some of the lightest and most fuel-efficient petrol cars, had asked for higher concessions to be given to small cars, saying compliance costs could finish off this segment.
The September 2025 draft added such a relief.
It said sub-4 metre petrol cars, with engines of up to 1,200 cc and an unladen weight of 909 kg or less, could deduct 3 g/km each from their CO2 figure.
This split the industry, with most carmakers opposing any weight-based relief.
Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles MD and CEO Shailesh Chandra had argued that easing rules on the basis of weight could compromise safety.
This relief has been removed from the final norms and the government has instead given a concession to small cars by adjusting the target-setting formula.
The September 2025 draft had used a reference weight of 1,170 kg and a steeper slope.
The final rules move the reference weight to 1,229 kg and flatten the slope.
As a result, the target for a small car, which would have been 54.1 g/km under the September 2025 draft after the relaxation, is now 63.7 g/km without the separate 3 g/km concession.

“The regulation recognises the contribution of multiple powertrain technologies and fuels encouraging multi-faceted R&D and innovation,” says Rahul Bharti, senior executive officer, corporate affairs at Maruti Suzuki.
A credit/debit mechanism is an improvisation over the previous Cafe-II regulation, he adds.
It also sells some strong hybrids, which count as 1.6x, and has entered the EV market with the eVitara though sales are yet to pick up.
Tata Motors built India’s EV market and is the largest electric player even today, a powertrain that gets three times the benefit.
“The continued recognition of zero-emission technologies reinforces the critical role of electrification in achieving India’s long-term decarbonisation objectives,” says Tata Motors’ Chandra.
Mahindra & Mahindra runs one of the heaviest fleets in the country and also has a diesel-heavy portfolio.
Its answer is EVs, a technology it has been investing in through its born-electric platform.

“At Mahindra, we are confident in our ability to meet these norms, backed by our sustained investments in technology, electrification and cleaner mobility,” says Velusamy R, president, automotive business, M&M.Hyundai India is betting on a mix.

Vikram Gulati, country head of Toyota Kirloskar Motor, the champion of strong hybrids in India, says the regulation is a big step forward and will play an important role in India’s march towards realising its goal of energy independence by 2047 as well as carbon net-neutral by 2070.
Smaller players selling fewer than 1,000 cars a year are exempt from the targets, but must report their fleet averages to the BEE.
Shenu Agarwal, president of auto industry body Siam, calls the targets “aggressive” and welcomes the “market-based compliance mechanism”.
JSW Motors, the Sajjan Jindal-led company that will likely launch its first car this year, is a clean-fuel carmaker and will have no issues with compliance.
CEO Ranjan Nayak says, “JSW Motors particularly welcomes the higher volume derogation factor of 3.0 for BEVs and REEVs, followed by 2.5 for PHEVs/eligible strong hybrids.

This appropriately recognises the greater contribution of battery-led technologies while allowing other electrified powertrains to play a role in the transition.” For component makers, a multi-fuel rulebook means more work across more platforms.
The industry is moving towards greater powertrain diversity rather than a sudden replacement of one technology with another, says Suresh D, group chief technology officer at Spark Minda.
He says suppliers must build capability in power electronics, battery management, vehicle control and electrical systems, while still serving conventional engines.
“Given that Cafe III is a fleet-level requirement, the industry will need solutions that can be scaled across multiple vehicle platforms rather than being restricted to a single model or powertrain.”

stories.title: Supreme Court Asks AG To Consider Plea To Enhance State Bar Councils' Strength
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today(October 1) requested the Attorney General, R. Venkataramani, to consider the plea of increasing the statutory limit of the State Bar Councils, which at present stands at 25 members as per Section 3(2)(b) of the Advocates Act, 1961.

A bench comprising Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana passed an order while hearing a writ petition filed by one advocate, who has contended that the statutory restriction of SBCs to 25 members was kept at a time when the 1961 Act was enacted.
But over time, the electorate has grown substantially.
For instance, he pointed out that the Bar Council of Delhi presently comprises 2 lakh registered advocates, which necessarily requires adequate and proportionate representation in the elected body.

The present writ petition, filed through AoR Nikhi Jain, has been preferred by one Rohit Pandey, who contested this year's Bar Council of Delhi Elections and secured 2,259 votes but fell short of 63.5 votes to be included among the 25 members of the SBC.

However, because of the Supreme Court's direction reserving 30% representation for women advocates in the SBCs, a low-ranking woman candidate was declared elected even though she secured only 265 votes.
As per his plea, the declaration of the said woman candidate as an elected member is contrary to the 1961 Act.
Supplementing this, Senior Advocate Vikas Singh and other senior advocates contended that Article 142 can't be used to pass a judicial order which is contrary to the statutory scheme.
Considering the brief submissions, the Court deemed it fit to pass a similar order it had passed on September 2.
Justice Bagchi, while passing the order, said: "We are absolutely aware of the judicial limitation, and that's why requesting the Attorney General."
The Court orally stated that if the AG takes a contrary view, the Court will consider.

On September 2, the Court, while hearing another writ petition on enhancement of seats in Bar Councils of Maharashtra and Goa, stated that the issue involves taking a policy decision and therefore requested the AG to treat the writ petition as a representation and take appropriate decisions in consultation with the SBCs.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Refuses To Interfere With Delhi High Court Ruling Against Ilaiyaraaja In 'En Iniya Pon Nilave' Copyright Dispute
stories.title: Supreme Court Refuses To Interfere With Delhi High Court Ruling Against Ilaiyaraaja In 'En Iniya Pon Nilave' Copyright Dispute
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today (01 October) has refused to interfere with the Delhi High Court's order restraining the use of a recreated version of the song En Iniya Pon Nilave, in a challenge brought up by music composer Ilaiyaraaja.
The bench, instead, clarified that the High Court's observations are prima facie.
A bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran was hearing the Special Leave Petition (SLP) filed by the music composer, against the Delhi High Court's Division Bench order.
The dispute pertains to Vels Film International Limited using a recreated version of the song.
Vels claimed a licence from Ilaiyaraaja under an agreement.
While Saregama India Limited contended that it owned the rights through an assignment from the film's original producer.
A Single Judge of the Delhi High Court granted Saregama an injunction, pursuant to which Ilaiyaraaja appealed before a Division Bench.

In May this year, a Division Bench of Justice C Hari Shankar and Justice Om Prakash Shukla dismissed the appeal, holding that his copyright is limited to the music of the song and does not extend to the lyrics or the sound recording.
Aggrieved by the High Court's ruling, a review petition was filed which was also dismissed, leading to the present SLP filed before the Supreme Court.
Before the Supreme Court, Senior Advocate C Aryama Sundaram submitted that the High Court's order had far reaching consequences.
“There are three other lawsuits which have been now filed based on this order,” he contended.

Invoking Section 13(4) of the Copyright Act, 1957, he argued that “the whole purpose of 13(4) is gone.” For context, Section 13(4) provides that copyright in a cinematograph film or sound recording does not affect the separate copyright in the underlying work.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves Green Energy Corridor Phase-III scheme
stories.title: Cabinet approves Green Energy Corridor Phase-III scheme
stories.summary: The initiative will give a push to India’s non-fossil capacity, help create more jobs: PM Modi
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved the Green Energy Corridor Phase-III (GEC-III) scheme.
This historic initiative will strengthen India’s Intra-State Transmission System (InSTS) to enable evacuation of up to 135 gigawatts (GW) of renewable energy across States/Union Territories.

Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, who briefed the media on Cabinet decisions, said the scheme also provides for deployment of 50 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) at the renewable energy (RE) developer/generator end or any other location of importance for grid flexibility to address intermittency, congestion, peak-hour curtailment and meet non-solar hour demand.
In a post on X, he said the move will create more jobs in manufacturing, construction and energy storage.
“Big push towards 900 GW non-fossil capacity by 2035.”
The presentation given by him described the scheme as PM Dhara (Developing Harmonised and Accelerated Renewable Energy Access).
The scheme will facilitate grid integration and power evacuation within the States and UTs.

The scheme is targeted to be set up by FY 2032-33 with a total project outlay of ₹1,86,405 crore, comprising ₹1,36,378 crore for the development of Intra-State Transmission Systems (InSTS) under GEC-III and ₹50,000 crore for 50 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), the release stated.
The scheme involves a total Central Financial Support of ₹54,082 crore.
The Central Financial Assistance (CFA) will help in offsetting the intra-State transmission charges and thus keep the power costs down.

All greenfield projects under the InSTS component will be implemented through Tariff Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) mode, while brownfield upgradation and network strengthening works will be executed under Cost Plus Basis (CPB).
The State Transmission Utilities will be the overall implementing agency, and Transmission Service Providers (TSPs) will participate under TBCB on a Build-Own-Operate-Maintain (BOOM) model.

stories.headline: India's growth holding up strong, Q3 GDP seen around 7.5 pc: Report
stories.title: India's growth holding up strong, Q3 GDP seen around 7.5 pc: Report
stories.summary: A report by HSBC Global Investment Research pointed to a string of strong economic indicators, including 8 per cent industrial production growth in August, 21 per cent growth in non-oil exports, around 25 per cent growth in public capital expenditure during April-August and 19 per cent credit growth in September.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A report by HSBC Global Investment Research pointed to a string of strong economic indicators, including 8 per cent industrial production growth in August, 21 per cent growth in non-oil exports, around 25 per cent growth in public capital expenditure during April-August and 19 per cent credit growth in September.
New Delhi: India's economy remains on a strong footing, supported by robust manufacturing activity, exports, investment and credit growth, a report said on Thursday.
Around 70 per cent of the indicators in its database showed positive growth in August, up from 52 per cent in the March-July period.
In addition, manufacturing has been particularly strong with September's flash PMI indicating a sharp rise in new orders.
Based on current trends, the report has estimated India's GDP growth at around 7.5 per cent in the third quarter.

The resilience has been broad-based despite disruptions from higher energy prices and adverse weather conditions, it said and added that consumption has remained stable helped by fuel tax cuts and a gradual pass-through of higher input costs.
Moreover, investment activity has been supported by public infrastructure spending as well as private sector investments in data centres, semiconductors and renewable energy.

Non-oil exports, especially electronics and engineering goods, have emerged as a key growth driver, the report said, highlighting that goods exports grew 20 per cent year-on-year in volume terms and 26 per cent in value terms in August.
It projects growth to moderate somewhat as the benefits of accommodative monetary policy and GST reductions fade.
However, HSBC warned that rising inflation, weather-related disruptions and higher borrowing costs could weigh on lower-income households and the informal sector.

It remains broadly optimistic, citing strong export momentum and the potential benefits of trade agreements with the UK and EU, noting that exports to the UK rose sharply after the implementation of the bilateral trade agreement.
"Overall, we are not too worried on growth," the report said.
